mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return tends to be positive due to lower real borrowing costs encouraging equity investment.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from the 20-day return during high-rate periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% in a single month is associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as market anticipates inflation pressure and rate hikes.
failure_condition: Across 10 such events, the 20-day forward return is not consistently negative (median p-value of t-tests > 0.3).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds its moving average by at least 2% for two consecutive months, it signals a strengthening supply-side momentum that is associated with positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > INDPRO_2mo_moving_avg by ≥ 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 5 such events, the 60-day forward return is not statistically higher than the 60-day return during neutral INDPRO periods (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) by over 10% in a month coincides with a negative S&P 20-day forward return as it signals labor market weakness and reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: Over 3 such episodes, the 20-day forward return is not consistently negative (median p-value > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both retail sales proxy (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) above their respective 5-day moving averages for three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 20-day forward return, reflecting dual-demand momentum.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > HOUST_5d_mavg & INDPRO > INDPRO_5d_mavg for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During 4 such interaction periods, the 20-day forward return is not statistically higher than baseline (p > 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% for four consecutive months is associated with positive S&P 60-day forward returns as it signals labor market tightness and wage growth.
failure_condition: Across 6 such episodes, the 60-day forward return is not significantly higher than during periods of higher unemployment (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer demand (RSAFS) falls by more than 5% in two consecutive months, it indicates weakening demand-side balance sheets and is associated with negative S&P 20-day forward returns as investors anticipate profit compression.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS month-over-month decrease > 5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 7 such events, the 20-day forward return is not consistently negative (median p-value > 0.25).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of unexpectedly high inflation (CPIAUCSL month-over-month surprise > 0.7%), the S&P 20-day forward return is negative due to anticipation of rate hikes, even if the underlying trend in FEDFUNDS is flat.
regime_hint: Unexpectedly high inflation while rates steady
failure_condition: In 8 such episodes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically lower than during periods of CPIAUCSL surprises ≤ 0.5% (p > 0.2).
